chapter: Opinions on playing and old New Orleans
title: The old days were better; copying Louis and having your own style
summary: Foster compares old whiskey and bands to today's, says Louis ruined trumpet players who copied his sound, and lists players with individual styles.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Because you had second best and best. See? It was like champagne, you got about nine different categories of champagne. You either had good champagne or no champagne back in those days. See? And you had the Clara wine, the Dago Red, it was good wine. You didn't have that Sherry wine. And the two wines was good, white wine and champagne. See? And that was good. But the same thing, same thing as the band. The Sweet Lou, sir.
The Sweet Lou, sir. Yeah. The Sweet Lou, sir. I used to like that. It was sweet. Yeah, I looked. Now, some of these, now all these trumpets, see Louie, Louie had ruined a many trumpet players.
He tried to copy those high notes now.

High notes. That guy was making mouthpieces. He got a nice trumpet player we had with us, Gus Aiken. Gus came a fool around, Gus is a very good musician too. He threw out his mouthpieces and he got one of them little small tinny tongs. You know what I mean? Mouthpieces they called him a chen mouthpiece. Ches mouthpiece, chen mother, hit him hand off.
Louie had one guy, I had one guy, he called June Clark.
Oh yeah, I've heard of him. He never knew him.

June Clark stuck his head out the window to get a cold so he could talk like Louie. And he still talked like Louie like today. See? And he can't help it. Can't help it. June was a nice trumpet player before he did all that stuff. Yeah. Oh, they would say. Yeah.

Now everything, see we haven't got, you don't find no individuals of the day. It's a copy of the day. See, no individuals, players of the day. You take the old guys, they didn't copy. Lyle had his style. Arnold Mottweiler, he had his style. See? Freddie had his style. Joan Pendleton had his style. Wiley had his style. Now when they come along with Buddy Petitian, Buddy had his style. Rainey, Rainey, Kid Rainey, he had his style.
Chris Kelly, did you hear him?

Well, all them guys had his style. Sam Morgan. Sam Morgan. They had his style. They had a different, they stayed in his style. See? You could be outside and hear that trumpet playing, I don't care, for blocks away, you could tell, well that's Sam, that's Sam Morgan's band, you could tell him what he's style, see? But today, everybody's trying to copy behind the other fella, you don't know who's style. Hey, you want to sit over here, wait and rest? No, no.
